title: How to Rekindle Desire in a Long Marriage
excerpt: Desire in a long marriage does not die because love faded. It cools because the conditions that fed it quietly disappeared, and the conditions can be rebuilt.
body:
Somewhere in a long marriage, often without either person deciding it, the fire goes low. Not out, usually. Low. You are partners, parents, co-managers of a complicated life, and the part of you that once could not keep your hands off this person has gone quiet, and you do not talk about it, because talking about it feels like an accusation, and not talking about it lets it keep cooling.

The church is often too embarrassed to help here, which is strange, because Scripture is not embarrassed at all. The Song of Songs is in the canon, an unblushing celebration of married desire, God's own answer to the lie that holiness is the enemy of passion. Paul tells married couples not to deprive one another, treating physical union as a mutual gift and a guarding of the marriage against the cold. The body is part of the covenant, not a distraction from it. So let us talk about it plainly.

## Desire is not a feeling that just shows up

The first lie we believe is that desire is spontaneous, that it should arrive on its own the way it did at the start, and if it does not, something is broken. At the start it was spontaneous because everything was new and you had endless unstructured time and your bodies had not yet been worn down by years of work and children and worry. That kind of desire was a gift of the season, and the season passed. It is not coming back on its own, and waiting for it is how a marriage waits itself into a permanent winter.

Mature desire is mostly responsive, not spontaneous. It does not show up first and then lead to closeness. It shows up because you created the closeness, and then the desire follows. This reverses everything. You do not wait to feel it before you tend it. You tend it, and the feeling comes back to meet you.

## Rebuild the conditions

Desire grows in specific soil, and in a long marriage that soil gets quietly paved over. Find what got paved and break it back up.

The first condition is attention. Desire needs to feel seen, and a spouse who has become invisible, who is only ever addressed about logistics, stops feeling like a person you want and starts feeling like a colleague. Look at your spouse again. Ask them a real question. Touch them in passing in a way that is not a request for anything. The Puritans, of all people, understood this, that romance is not a feeling that happens to you but a fire that has to be fed by attention and kindness, on purpose, and that love left untended cools.

The second condition is non-utilitarian touch. In a long marriage, touch becomes entirely functional, especially in the years of small children, all of it carrying and feeding and the brief logistics of the bed. When the only touch is functional, the body forgets the other language. Bring back the touch that asks for nothing, the long hug in the kitchen, the hand held on a walk. The body has to be reminded that it is desired and not just deployed.

The third condition is separateness, which sounds wrong and is true. Desire needs a little distance to cross. Two people who have fused completely, who do everything together and have no separate self left, can lose the gap that desire arches across. Have a life of your own, an interest, a friendship, a competence your spouse admires from a small distance. Watching your spouse be good at something, alive in something that is theirs, can reignite the wanting that total togetherness flattened.

## Talk about it without the accusation

The conversation feels dangerous because any version of I want more can land as you are failing me. So aim it at the marriage, not at your spouse. I miss us. I miss this part of us, and I want to find our way back to it, and I do not blame you for where it went, because I let it go too. Self-implication disarms the conversation. The moment your spouse hears that you are not prosecuting them, that you are inside the problem with them, the defensiveness drops and the real conversation can start.

And listen for what cooled it. Sometimes the desire went low because of resentment that never got cleared, or exhaustion that never got relieved, or a hurt around the body that never got spoken. Desire is honest. It often will not return until the thing blocking it gets named. The bedroom is frequently where the unaddressed rest of the marriage shows up.

## Guard the conditions like they matter

The practical part is unromantic and necessary. You will not stumble into the conditions. You have to protect them. A regular time when you are both awake enough to want each other and not running on the fumes of an exhausting day. A door that locks. A phone left in the other room. The couples who keep this alive across decades are not the ones who got lucky. They are the ones who treated it as something worth tending and refused to let it be the thing that always got cut when life got busy.

## This week

Do two small things. First, touch your spouse once a day this week in a way that asks for nothing, a real hug, a hand held, thirty seconds, no agenda. You are rebuilding the language. Second, sometime this week, say the gentle version of the true thing: I miss us, and I want to find our way back. Do not aim for a transformed marriage by Friday. Aim to break up a little of the paved ground, and to say the thing you have both been afraid to say. The fire did not go out. It went low for lack of tending, and tending is something you can begin again tonight.
